title: SiteOne Crawler: Rust-Powered SEO Audit Tool with LLM Review
summary: SiteOne Crawler launches as an open-source Rust web crawler for SEO audits and content analysis, featuring optional LLM-powered quality reviews.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- SiteOne Crawler debuts as an open-source Rust web crawler designed for SEO audits and content analysis workflows.
- The tool features optional LLM integration to automate content quality reviews alongside traditional crawling metrics and reporting.
- Built with Rust for performance, the crawler aims to help developers and SEO teams streamline site audits at scale.


A new open-source web crawler built in Rust has officially launched on Hacker News, targeting developers and SEO professionals who need efficient site auditing capabilities. SiteOne Crawler combines traditional crawling functionality with optional large language model integration for automated[content quality](https://emergent.sh/ai-agent-builder/content-optimization) assessment, offering a modern approach to technical SEO and content analysis workflows.


## Core Crawling Capabilities


The crawler leverages Rust's performance characteristics to handle large-scale website audits. It systematically traverses web pages, collecting structural data, metadata, and content elements that inform SEO optimization decisions. The tool generates reports on common technical issues including broken links, duplicate content, missing meta descriptions, and page load performance metrics.


Unlike many existing crawlers that rely on Python or Node.js, the Rust implementation prioritizes speed and memory efficiency. This architectural choice enables the tool to process enterprise-scale websites with thousands of pages without the resource overhead typical of interpreted languages.


## Optional LLM Review Feature


What distinguishes SiteOne Crawler from traditional audit tools is its optional integration with large language models. When enabled, the LLM component analyzes crawled content for quality signals including readability, topical relevance, keyword usage, and alignment with SEO best practices. This automation layer helps content teams identify pages that may need revision or improvement.


The LLM review operates as a modular add-on rather than a core requirement, allowing teams to run standard technical crawls independently or augment them with AI-powered content analysis based on project needs. According to the project documentation, users can configure which language model to use and customize the evaluation criteria.


## Open Source Architecture


The project is available under an open-source license, enabling developers to inspect the codebase, contribute improvements, or customize the crawler for specialized use cases. The Rust ecosystem provides built-in concurrency primitives that the crawler uses to parallelize requests efficiently while respecting server rate limits and robots.txt directives.


The tool's modular design separates crawling logic from analysis and reporting components. This separation allows teams to extend functionality through plugins or integrate the crawler into existing[SEO automation](https://emergent.sh/ai-automation-builder/seo) pipelines and CI/CD workflows.


## Release and Availability


SiteOne Crawler was officially launched on November 1, 2026, with the initial release posted to Hacker News as a Show HN submission. The project is immediately available for download and deployment, with documentation covering installation, configuration, and basic usage patterns for common audit scenarios.


The open-source nature of the release encourages community contributions to expand crawler capabilities, improve LLM integration options, and add support for additional content management systems and web frameworks.


## What This Means


The launch of SiteOne Crawler reflects growing interest in combining traditional SEO tooling with AI capabilities. By implementing the core crawler in Rust, the project addresses performance limitations that have constrained Python-based alternatives. The optional LLM review feature positions the tool at the intersection of technical SEO and content quality automation, a space where many teams currently rely on manual processes or disconnected tool chains. For developers managing large content inventories, this release offers a potential consolidation point for audit workflows.
